Chapter 11 environmental permanova

We test whether environmental α-diversity (Hill h0/h1/h2 of land-cover) relates to microbiome β-diversity (Bray–Curtis), and visualise relationships (e.g., NMDS axes vs. Hill metrics) and distance-matrix structure.

11.1 Load data

Note: Load all required data objects including sample metadata, beta diversity matrices, and Hill diversity metrics from the RData files created in previous chapters.

11.2 Data preparation

Note: Filter out sample EHI01340 from the metadata and Hill diversity data. This sample was removed because it could not be mapped to MAGs, ensuring consistency across downstream analyses.

sample_metadata <- sample_metadata %>% dplyr::filter(sample != "EHI01340")
hill_long       <- hill_long       %>% dplyr::filter(id     != "EHI01340")

Note: Transform Hill diversity data from long to wide format, creating separate columns for each Hill diversity metric (env_hill_h0, env_hill_h1, env_hill_h2). Join with sample metadata to create a combined metadata object for downstream analyses.

11.3 Helper functions

Note: Helper function to align metadata with distance matrices. This eliminates code duplication when aligning metadata for multiple distance matrices. Defined early as it’s needed by multiple analysis sections.

Note: Optimized helper function that accepts pre-calculated NMDS object instead of recalculating. This eliminates redundant NMDS calculations when creating multiple plots.

11.4 Ordination analysis

Note: Extract distance matrices from beta diversity objects for use in ordination analyses. These matrices represent Bray-Curtis dissimilarities between samples at different diversity orders.

Note: Calculate all NMDS ordinations once upfront. These are expensive operations (trymax = 500 iterations each) and were previously calculated redundantly 3+ times. This optimization saves significant computation time.

Note: Align metadata with each distance matrix using the helper function. This ensures proper sample order matching for ordination and visualization.

11.5 Grouping variables

Note: Create grouping variables for environmental Hill diversity metrics. Calculate medians once to avoid redundant calculations. Split into tertiles (Low, Mid, High) and median-based groups (Low, High) for visualization and statistical testing.

Note: Verify the grouping variables were created correctly by displaying frequency tables. This ensures balanced group sizes for downstream analyses.


 Low  Mid High 
  30   22   20 

High  Low 
  27   45

11.6 PERMANOVA analysis

Note: Define function to run PERMANOVA tests for each environmental Hill diversity metric (h0, h1, h2) against beta diversity distance matrices. The function aligns metadata with distance matrix samples, ensures sample order matches, and performs PERMANOVA with 999 permutations for each Hill metric. This eliminates code duplication when testing multiple beta diversity matrices.

11.7 Mantel tests

Note: Test correlations between environmental Hill diversity and beta diversity using Mantel tests. This is more appropriate than linear regression on NMDS axes since it tests relationships directly on distance matrices, which is the appropriate scale for beta diversity analysis.

11.8 Betadisper tests

Note: Test for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions (variance) across Hill diversity tertile groups using betadisper. This tests whether groups differ in their dispersion around the centroid, which is an assumption of PERMANOVA. Tests all three beta diversity matrices for consistency.

11.10 Visualization

Associations between environmental α-diversity (Hill h0/h1/h2) and microbiome ordination (NMDS1/2), with fitted vectors and a subset heatmap of Bray–Curtis distances.

Note: Create combined scatterplots showing relationships between all environmental Hill diversity metrics and NMDS ordination axes. This provides a comprehensive view of how environmental diversity relates to microbiome β-diversity ordination. Uses loess smoothing instead of linear regression, which is more appropriate for potentially non-linear relationships.

Note: Fit environmental Hill diversity vectors (h0, h1, h2) onto the q0 NMDS ordination using envfit. This tests the correlation between environmental variables and ordination axes, displaying significant vectors as arrows on the ordination plot. Improved visualization using ggplot2 for consistency with other plots.

Note: Create an improved heatmap visualization of Bray-Curtis dissimilarity matrix with sample grouping information. This shows clustering patterns in microbiome β-diversity and how they relate to environmental Hill diversity groups. Uses all samples (or a representative subset if too large) with grouping annotations.

#abundance analysis of micrb community in diffrent enviroment diversitys

This chapter analyzes differential abundance of microbial genomes between samples with low and high environmental diversity (Hill diversity metrics h0, h1, h2). We use ANCOM-BC2 to identify significantly differentially abundant genomes and visualize results with barplots and volcano plots.

11.11 Load data

Note: Load sample metadata, genome count data, and Hill diversity metrics from RData files created in previous chapters. Filter out sample EHI01340 which was removed because it could not be mapped to MAGs, ensuring consistency across downstream analyses.

Note: Transform Hill diversity data from long to wide format, creating separate columns for each Hill diversity metric (env_hill_h0, env_hill_h1, env_hill_h2). Join with sample metadata to create a combined metadata object for downstream analyses.

11.12 Data preparation

Note: Create grouping variables for each Hill diversity metric (q0, q1, q2). Split samples into tertiles (Low, Mid, High) based on environmental Hill diversity, then filter to keep only Low and High groups for two-group comparisons. For each q value, create filtered metadata and genome count matrices containing only samples in Low/High groups and genomes present in at least one sample.

n filtered_inputs = 3 
q=0 nLow=30 nHigh=20 genomes=1750
q=1 nLow=25 nHigh=17 genomes=1522
q=2 nLow=24 nHigh=17 genomes=1514

11.13 Structural zeros analysis

Note: Identify structural zeros - genomes that are completely absent (zero counts) in one group (Low or High) but present in the other. This is important for ANCOM-BC2 analysis as structural zeros can be handled explicitly. For each q value, calculate which genomes are structurally absent in Low vs High groups and compute group means for genomes that are present in only one group.

Note: Create UpSet plot using UpSetR to visualize the intersection of genomes present in Low and High environmental diversity groups. The plot shows unique genomes in each group and shared genomes, with colors indicating group membership.

11.14 Differential abundance analysis

11.14.1 Build phyloseq objects

Note: Create phyloseq objects for each q value (q0, q1, q2) containing OTU table (genome counts), taxonomy table, and sample metadata. Counts are kept as integers with zeros allowed, as ANCOM-BC2 can handle zeros without requiring pseudocounts. Sample metadata includes the grouping variable (Low/High) for each Hill diversity metric.

11.14.2 Run ANCOM-BC2 analysis

Note: Perform ANCOM-BC2 differential abundance testing for each q value, comparing Low vs High environmental diversity groups. The analysis uses structural zero modeling (struc_zero=TRUE) to properly handle genomes absent in one group. Version-adaptive code handles differences between ANCOMBC package versions. Results include log fold-changes, p-values, and adjusted p-values for each genome.

11.14.3 Visualize differential abundance results

Note: Extract significantly differentially abundant genomes (p < 0.05) from ANCOM-BC2 results and create visualizations. Barplots show log2 fold-changes for significant genomes, ordered by effect size and colored by phylum. Volcano plots show all tested genomes with log2 fold-change on x-axis and -log10(p-value) on y-axis, highlighting significant hits. Both visualizations are created for each q value (q0, q1, q2).

Note: Alternative barplot visualization using genome identifiers instead of taxon names. This provides a different view of the same differential abundance results, useful for identifying specific genomes of interest.

11.15 Alternative ANCOM-BC2 analysis with structural zeros

Note: Run an alternative ANCOM-BC2 analysis with additional structural zero handling parameters. This analysis uses a random effects model (rand_formula=“~1”) and different parameter settings including Holm p-value adjustment, pseudo-sensitivity analysis, and explicit structural zero detection. This provides a complementary view to the main analysis and may identify additional differentially abundant genomes.

Note: Extract and clean results from the alternative ANCOM-BC2 analysis with structural zeros. Filter for significantly differentially abundant genomes (p < 0.05), join with taxonomy information, and create cleaned tables ready for visualization or further analysis. Results are organized by log fold-change for easy interpretation.

11.16 Load data

Note: Load sample metadata, genome count data, and Hill diversity metrics from RData files created in previous chapters. These data objects will be used for diversity and abundance analysis comparing samples with low and high environmental diversity.

11.17 Data preparation

Note: Exclude outlier sample EHI01340 from all datasets. Transform Hill diversity data from long to wide format and join with sample metadata. Choose a Hill diversity metric (default: h1, exponential Shannon) to split samples into tertiles. Filter to keep only Low and High groups (excluding Mid) for two-group comparisons. Ensure sample metadata and genome count matrices are aligned, keeping only samples present in both datasets and genomes with at least one non-zero count.

# --- Configuration: outlier sample to exclude ------------------------------
outlier_sample <- "EHI01340"

# Check if outlier sample exists (may already be excluded in previous chapters)
if (!outlier_sample %in% sample_metadata$sample) {
  message("Note: Outlier sample '", outlier_sample, 
          "' not found in sample_metadata (likely already excluded in previous chapters).")
}

# drop the outlier sample everywhere (safe even if already excluded)
sample_metadata <- sample_metadata %>% filter(sample != outlier_sample)

# Optimized: Filter genome counts in one pass - select valid samples and filter zero rows
valid_sample_cols <- intersect(sample_metadata$sample, colnames(genome_counts_filt))
genome_counts_filt <- genome_counts_filt %>%
  select(genome, all_of(valid_sample_cols)) %>%
  filter(rowSums(across(-genome, ~ .x != 0), na.rm = TRUE) > 0)

# Validate filtering results
if (nrow(sample_metadata) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No samples remaining after filtering. Check sample_metadata.")
}
if (nrow(genome_counts_filt) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No genomes remaining after filtering. Check genome_counts_filt.")
}

# --- choose which Hill order to split on ----------------------------------
# use "h1" by default (exp-Shannon). Change to "h0" or "h2" if you prefer.
q_choice <- "h1"

# Validate q_choice format
valid_q_choices <- c("h0", "h1", "h2")
if (!q_choice %in% valid_q_choices) {
  stop("Error: q_choice must be one of: ", paste(valid_q_choices, collapse = ", "))
}

# Validate hill_long exists and has data
if (!exists("hill_long") || nrow(hill_long) == 0) {
  stop("Error: hill_long is missing or empty.")
}

# Optimized: Build Hill-wide and join with metadata in one pipeline
hill_col <- paste0("env_hill_", q_choice)

hill_wide <- hill_long %>%
  filter(id != outlier_sample) %>%
  rename(sample = id) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = sample,
              names_from = q,
              values_from = value,
              names_glue = "env_hill_{q}")

# Validate pivot_wider results
if (!hill_col %in% colnames(hill_wide)) {
  stop("Error: Hill diversity column '", hill_col, "' not found after pivot_wider. ",
       "Available columns: ", paste(colnames(hill_wide), collapse = ", "))
}

# Optimized: Join and filter missing Hill data in one step
meta_hill <- sample_metadata %>%
  left_join(hill_wide, by = "sample") %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[hill_col]]))  # Remove samples with missing Hill diversity data

# Report if any samples were excluded
n_excluded_hill <- nrow(sample_metadata) - nrow(meta_hill)
if (n_excluded_hill > 0) {
  warning("Found ", n_excluded_hill, " samples with missing Hill diversity data. These were excluded.")
}

# Validate we have enough samples for tertiles (need at least 3)
if (nrow(meta_hill) < 3) {
  stop("Error: Insufficient samples (", nrow(meta_hill), ") for creating tertiles. Need at least 3 samples.")
}

group_col <- paste0("env_group_q", substr(q_choice, 2, 2))  # env_group_q1, etc.

# tertiles → keep only Low/High (drop Mid) and fix factor order Low < High
# Use tryCatch to handle edge cases in cut_number
meta_hill <- tryCatch({
  meta_hill %>%
    mutate(
      !!group_col := ggplot2::cut_number(.data[[hill_col]],
                                        3, labels = c("Low","Mid","High"))
    ) %>%
    filter(.data[[group_col]] %in% c("Low","High")) %>%
    mutate(!!group_col := factor(.data[[group_col]], levels = c("Low","High")))
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error creating tertiles with cut_number: ", e$message, 
       ". This may occur if there are too few unique values in ", hill_col)
})

# Validate group creation
if (nrow(meta_hill) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No samples remaining after filtering to Low/High groups.")
}

# Validate group creation
group_counts <- table(meta_hill[[group_col]], useNA = "no")
if (any(group_counts == 0)) {
  stop("Error: One or both groups (Low/High) are empty after filtering. ",
       paste(names(group_counts), group_counts, sep = "=", collapse = ", "))
}

# Optimized: Keep only samples present in both datasets in one pass
valid_samples <- intersect(meta_hill$sample, colnames(genome_counts_filt))
if (length(valid_samples) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No overlapping samples between meta_hill and genome_counts_filt.")
}

# Filter both datasets to valid samples
meta_hill <- meta_hill %>% filter(sample %in% valid_samples)
genome_counts_filt <- genome_counts_filt %>% 
  select(genome, all_of(valid_samples)) %>%
  # Re-filter genomes to ensure they're still present after sample filtering
  filter(rowSums(across(-genome, ~ .x != 0), na.rm = TRUE) > 0)

# Final validation
if (nrow(meta_hill) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No samples remaining after final filtering.")
}

cat("N Low / High = ",
    sum(meta_hill[[group_col]] == "Low"), " / ",
    sum(meta_hill[[group_col]] == "High"), "\n", sep = "")
## N Low / High = 25 / 17
